findings.body:
The USER_FORCED_RESET branch in this diagram only lists applied_label + prior stamp + label absent. Runtime `run_iar_pre_llm` also requires `label_fetch_ok` (PR-labels REST succeeded) so a GitHub 5xx empty list cannot wipe fingerprint memory. Operators copying this diagram will miss the fifth guard that `docs/ITERATION_AWARENESS.md` § 8.5 treats as load-bearing.

```suggestion
│   ├── (USER_FORCED_RESET override) ← only when ALL FIVE hold:
│   │                                    applied_label configured, prior_state
│   │                                    exists, prior_state.reviewed_label_applied,
│   │                                    label_fetch_ok (PR-labels REST succeeded),
│   │                                    and applied_label absent from the returned
│   │                                    list. Clears prior_state to None and
│   │                                    forces new_lines_pct=0.0.
```

`skipped` is still described as label-gate only, but this PR adds `skip-review-label` and both `action.yml` and `README.md` already say the output covers label/author gate **or** the emergency bypass. Setup-skill drift breaks the “any agent can answer setup questions” promise (AGENTS.md Rule #7).

```suggestion
| `skipped` | Whether the run was skipped without invoking the LLM (`true`/`false`). Set when EITHER the label/author gate suppressed the run OR the configured `skip-review-label` emergency bypass fired. |
```

“baseline (IAR-off) path” reads like the removed opt-out switch. After unconditional IAR, failure degrades to a baseline review with empty IAR outputs / no marker annotation — not an off mode. Worth aligning with the rest of this PR’s wording sweep.

```suggestion
- **Never crashes the reviewer.** Both `run_iar_pre_llm` and `run_iar_post_llm` are wrapped in `try/except` at the call site in `main()`. On any IAR failure the reviewer falls back to the baseline review path (no IAR marker annotation / empty IAR outputs) and logs the exception — the CI check still gets a review, IAR just skips this run.
```

summary:
## Verdict

Solid, high-stakes feature landing. Runtime IAR / skip-label / USER_FORCED_RESET invariants look correct and well locked by tests; remaining issues are operator-facing doc/contract drift, not merge-blocking security bugs.

## What I verified

**Security / contract rails (pass):**
- Stdlib-only imports; no `shell=True`; `git show` paths go through `safe_repo_path`.
- Marker contracts preserved (`REVIEW_MARKER`, provider marker, IAR state tags).
- New optional inputs only (`skip-review-label` + 4 IAR knobs + 5 IAR outputs) — no removals/renames of existing public surface.
- Secrets still registered; skip path does not stamp `applied-label`, does not mutate IAR state, runs before collapse/LLM.
- Skip-label collision guard covers gate / applied / escape (case-insensitive).
- USER_FORCED_RESET five-condition guard is present in code (`reviewed_label_applied` + `label_fetch_ok` + configured/absent/prior).
- Critical-always-surfaces rail is hardcoded in `dedupe_findings_against_prior`; cap truncation uses `_sort_findings_criticals_first` on both exhaustive and agent-runner paths.
- Marker fetch keeps tier-2 minimized-with-state fallback, author filter, and provider isolation.
- `try/except` wraps both IAR pre/post call sites; `write_all_outputs` always empties the 5 IAR outputs first.
- `reviewed_label_applied` is written after observed `gh_apply_label` via `compute_reviewed_label_applied` three-signal OR.
- Escape short-circuit is skipped on `USER_FORCED_RESET` in `dispatch_policy`.
- Three-dot range hash / safety-net denominator match the PR-visible diff contract.

**Coverage:** dedicated IAR suites + skip renderer/collision tests + failure-fallback suite look aligned with the load-bearing contracts. Manual smoke tests for reset/skip are still open in the PR body (expected for dogfood).
